messages.author: 16644d25568cd19d
messages.subject: Model identification
parts:
Hi,
I'm trying to run a 3 factor model (35 items) as well as a higher order 3F model with 221 cases.
Both have come up with the error that it is not positive definite.
I notice an item (18) which was reverse worded/scored has very low R Square and negative std.lv in both models.
I checked correlations and this item had low, nonsignificant correlations with other items in the scale. However, when I ran the models without this item, still not positive definite. There was no multicollinearity (highest correlation was .6 between items).
Is this just an issue of not enough cases, or is there something else I need to be doing to get these models to run?
Thanks, Nicole

messages.author: 9b7a59c6f2d552cc
messages.subject: Re: Model identification
parts:
Nicole
there are other causes for not positive definite beside high inter-correlations.
Perhaps there is an item with negative error variance within your model that is causing problems. 
the sample size should be ok in that your case to variable ratio is greater than 5:1
Perhaps you should test each factor separately before merging them into one model.

here are some references you could consult for alternative causes and solutions.
Chen, F., Bollen, K. A., Paxton, P., Curran, P. J., & Kirby, J. B. (2001). Improper solutions in structural equation models: Causes, consequences, and strategies. Sociological Methods & Research, 29(4), 468-508. https://doi.org/10.1177/0049124101029004003
Dillon, W. R., Kumar, A., & Mulani, N. (1987). Offending estimates in covariance structure analysis: Comments on the causes of and solutions to Heywood cases. Psychological Bulletin, 101(1), 126-135.
Gerbing, D. W., & Anderson, J. C. (1987). Improper solutions in the analysis of covariance structures: Their interpretability and a comparison of alternate respecifications. Psychometrika, 52(1), 99-111. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF02293958
Kolenikov, S., & Bollen, K. A. (2012). Testing Negative Error Variances: Is a Heywood Case a Symptom of Misspecification? Sociological Methods & Research, 41, 124-167. https://doi.org/10.1177/0049124112442138

messages.subject: Re: Model identification
parts:
Hi Gavin,
Thanks for the information. I've had another look at the data and the readings you suggested.
The scale I've developed has 35 items, when I run the self-report version the models are great.
However, when I run the exact same models with informant participants (the same number of participants, they are just rating the self-report participants), none of the models work, I receive the not positive definite error.
I ran the factors separately, but still no luck unfortunately. As far as I can tell there is no negative error variance, so I'm a bit stuck.
Any advice on where to go from here would be great (I'm not an overly skilled use of R, so not sure what to do next).
Thanks, Nicole

parts:
Thanks Gavin,
I tried a few things:
the higher order factor didn't work unfortunately.
I also ran the 3 factors separately. Factor 2 and 3 worked fine, but factor 1 seems to be where the negative error variance is located.
I tried running factor 1 removing one item at a time to see if I could identify a problematic item, but I still got the not positive definite error each time, so I'm really not sure where this area is coming from.
I don't think it's a sample size issue, as I've run the self-report version and it was all fine, with the same number of cases.
Thanks, Nicole
